title: Distributed Internet of things equipment identification method and system based on federal learning
assignee: Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics

pse.problem: Challenge in developing an effective internet of things equipment identification algorithm due to privacy concerns, regulations, and transmission loads, which makes it often not feasible or prohibited to directly transmit data from an edge device to a central server to train a unified device fingerprinting model.
pse.solution_function: Federated learning-based distributed device identification algorithm that enables cooperative processing of the traffic of internet of things devices distributed on different edge devices, while protecting privacy by periodically exchanging local model parameters without sharing original data.
pse.solution_structure: Edge devices (e.g., mobile phones, medical care equipment, wearable equipment), a server model, and the locally trained models at each edge device.
pse.solution_implementation: Federated learning algorithm that performs knowledge distillation in a generative manner by initializing a server model, weighting integrated local model with metadata from the logic-vector output of the local model, and sharing the metadata between edge devices.
pse.effect: Improved internet of things equipment identification accuracy while preserving privacy and reducing the cost of exchanging model parameters
